page: Amazon Web Services r8a.metal-24xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance powered by a 96-core AMD EPYC 9R45 processor running at up to 4.5 GHz. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture with a 1:1 physical-core-to-vCPU ratio and disabled simultaneous multithreading, it provides 96 total execution threads. The system features 768 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 6 GHz, yielding an 8 GB per core memory allocation. Network connectivity is delivered via a 40 Gbps baseline interface. Local NVMe SSD storage is not bundled, requiring external network-attached storage for persistent host data.

Benchmark results place the instance in the top tier for multi-core and single-core CPU throughput, as well as memory bandwidth. In stress-ng testing, multi-core CPU score reached 349,628.66, and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measured 521.03 GB/sec. The hardware instruction set includes AVX-512 extensions and hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions. Application-level performance metrics show high throughput across key enterprise workloads, achieving 235.68 million Redis SET operations per second and 117.49 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

The high memory capacity per core combined with bare-metal execution eliminates hypervisor overhead, delivering predictable latency and resource isolation for dense memory workloads. Without local storage or discrete GPU hardware, the instance relies on remote block storage for state persistence and is unsuited for accelerated graphics or compute pipeline processing. However, its high DDR5 memory bandwidth and core density make it well suited for high-throughput in-memory datastores, large database deployments, enterprise software compilation, and big data ETL processing.
description: Amazon Web Services r8a.metal-24xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance featuring 96 physical AMD EPYC 9R45 CPU cores operating at 4.5 GHz. It includes 768 GB of high-speed 6 GHz DDR5 memory, offering an 8 GB per core allocation without hypervisor overhead. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor supports AVX-512 extensions and cryptographic hardware acceleration. Networking capability is configured at a 40 Gbps baseline. The host does not include local NVMe storage or discrete GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate top-tier performance in multi-core execution, memory bandwidth, and database throughput, including 235.68 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance provides strong cost efficiency for high-density, memory-bound workloads that do not require local ephemeral disk storage, making it suitable for large in-memory databases, real-time analytics, big data ETL processing, and parallel software compilation.
